stem.text: The Michaelis-Menten constant for an enzyme-catalysed reaction is referred to as $K_\text{m}$, and the maximum velocity of such a reaction is known as $V_\text{max}$.
Which statement about $K_\text{m}$ and $V_\text{max}$ is correct?

A.text: An enzyme with a high value of $K_\text{m}$ can reach its $V_\text{max}$ at a low substrate concentration.

B.text: An enzyme with a high value of $K_\text{m}$ has a high affinity to its substrate.

C.text: An enzyme with a low value of $K_\text{m}$ can reach its $V_\text{max}$ at a high substrate concentration.

D.text: An enzyme with a low value of $K_\text{m}$ has a high affinity to its substrate.
